author: Vivian Nguyen
title: Melrose High appoints Cedrick C. Wilson as new head football coach - NewsBreak
text:
By Vivian Nguyen No media credit provided. ,
9 hours ago MEMPHIS, Tenn. — The Memphis-Shelby County Schools (MSCS) announced it appointed a new head football coach at Melrose High School on Wednesday.
MSCS said that alumnus Cedrick C. Wilson is the new head coach for the Golden Wildcats after the Commercial Appeal reported that brothers Gerald Morrow and Jarrett Morrow were resigning in January.
Cedrick C. Wilson Courtesy: MSCS Melrose High School said Wilson is known as “a native of the Historic Orange Mound community.”
“It is an honor to return home and lead the program that shaped me,” said Coach Wilson. “Melrose means family, tradition, and excellence. I am committed to building champions on the field, in the classroom, and in the community.”
Penny Hardaway dismisses senior player from Memphis Tigers According to MSCS, in 2001, Wilson was drafted into the NFL and played for the San Francisco 49ers and later the Pittsburgh Steelers.
They said his professional career includes more than 2,300 receiving yards and earning a championship ring in Super Bowl XL in 2006 with the Steelers.
“Following his NFL career, Wilson returned to Memphis to serve the next generation of scholars and athletes,” said MSCS. “He currently supports students as an RTI²-B Behavioral Specialist with Memphis-Shelby County Schools, serving both Melrose High School and Hanley Elementary School.”
The high school said they are celebrating the new chapter and look forward to what Coach Wilson will bring to the Golden Wildcats.
